utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Where is the mistake? In the document, it says "HV Kotromanic Brigade," and apart from a misprint, that is what is in the transcript. Hrvatinic, we had before, that is a different brigade, so here Kotromanic is correct. No. Then it's incorrect on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English translation misstates it. That was an office translation. It had to be done quickly, and the quantities were overwhelming. So there was an error in the original text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So the error is between the documents and not with the transcript, primarily. Thank you. I'm sorry, I didn't grasp it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What I said on line 15 of page 91, it is a translation, a written translation, not interpretation. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pinter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall be submitting a corrected version for tomorrow's hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: General, can we now please go to 3D01100. No date, but it is obviously from August 1993. You signed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same order. This independent battalion from Klis is the battalion from over near Konjic that came under attack by the BH Army in April and was crushed. People were killed, expelled, and so on and so forth. And then those men -- it's true what it says here. Disciplinary steps taken against perpetrators are to be carried out with no further delay, as well as any other orders. All of this, Ms. Nika, Your Honours, looks very nice when we see it in a document like that and when it's signed. But when you actually see those people, the people involved, when you talk to them, when you see the amount of sheer energy emanating from those people, the grief over their dead, and their families being expelled, then the order takes on an entirely different meaning. All right, I wrote the order. I wrote about the disciplinary steps to be taken and all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, let me return to the question I put about the military prosecutor, the SIS, and military police. In this document, you are asking for disciplinary measures. Fine, nothing to say. You did your job very well. But when you heard that detainees had been used on the front-line, why didn't you ask for disciplinary measures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, disciplinary measures -- commanders at each of the levels have the power to take certain disciplinary measures within the HVO, but disciplinary measures alone; nothing beyond that, nothing more serious, in terms of more serious offences. In this case, I know exactly who is carrying out my order. And I request that Marko Stanic take disciplinary measures against persons failing to comply. When men were taken to the front-line to dig trenches, I knew of no way in which the ban on doing that was actually violated or by whom. This is all happening in the staff. And then you ask, Who did this? No one will ever stand up, come forward and say, I did that. So what happens is you need to launch an investigation because, unfortunately, no one will be coming forward to say, Yesterday, I did this and that, so now you do what you have to do. No. Instead, you need to launch an investigation. As far as investigations were concerned, the Main Staff or, indeed, I, myself, had no ability whatsoever to take any steps in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Pinter, we have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, in view of how you have presented yourself, with your study of psychologist, with your power over everyone, with your enormous authority, within half an hour you would have known, if you had actually put your mind to it, because you could have known where they had come from. There were traces. They came not out of the blue. They did not fall from the sky. But you did not care; isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not the truth, Judge Trechsel. Read all of my actions from the beginning to the very end in this case. How do you get this idea? Because I studied psychology, that I would have been able to track down the perpetrator, or, indeed, that I had the power to do that? What I'm telling you is that when I found out about the existence of a camp over in Dretelj, I did what I did. Once I had found out, I went there, armed, and I set those people free. When I realised that someone was stealing a vehicle right there in front of me, I took a gun to it. A man like that. Do you not think I would have punished whoever I knew for sure was taking people to perform labour at the front-line? Take all of it, take all of the documents, and there are at least 115 in this case alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: A question -- the previous question was asked by Judge Trechsel and not by Judge Antonetti, and so, therefore, the transcript should be changed and corrected accordingly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise if I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, it's nearly 7.00, three minutes to go. You know this week we sit in the afternoons. Therefore, we shall resume -- reconvene tomorrow at 2.15. You have used 35 hours and 30 minutes. I'm saying this to the Defence counsel. So, in principle, at this pace we should be able to finish the week -- so, in principle, we should conclude the week with you without any problem, because you must have over four hours left. But, of course, all this brings about questions, and we have to take the time we need. I wish you all a good evening. We shall reconvene tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of June, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
